title: SKU-aware microbatch-adaptive kernel arbitration for MIG-isolated H100/L40S/A10 fleets
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: We observe 6-18% tail latency regressions and 10-25% throughput variance across mixed fleets (H100, L40S, A10) when MIG partitions are active and dynamic clock governors change under thermal pressure. Root cause signals point to suboptimal kernel variant selection plus microbatch sizing decisions made without SKU- or partition-awareness during prefill and decode phases.

Goal: Implement a lightweight arbitration layer in the serving runtime that chooses a kernel variant + microbatch size + clock-hint at request time based on (a) GPU SKU, (b) MIG partition size, (c) current clock headroom telemetry, and (d) sequence-length distribution. The arbitration should be pluggable, low-overhead (<250us decision wall time), and support deterministic fallbacks for predictable SLAs.
tasks: Instrument runtime to expose per-slice clock headroom and partition share metrics to scheduler
Design kernel candidate ranking heuristic that weights latency, throughput, and memory headroom per SKU
Implement microbatch-sizing policy tied to kernel hint and current KV-cache occupancy for prefill vs decode
Add safe-fallback path that forces conservative kernel and clock hints under thermal/telemetry anomalies
Integrate with existing autoscaling telemetry dashboard and add experiment flags
Run cross-sku perf sweep (H100 L40S A10) using live traces and synthetic token-length distributions
Produce runbook entries for ops: when to force safe mode, signals for rollout rollback
progress_updates: 2026-02-26: Spike: collected perf traces across H100/L40S/A10 with MIG=1/2/3 partitions. Confirmed variance correlates with partition size and active clock governor transitions (nvml telemetry).

2026-03-02: Prototype arbitration decision path added to dev branch. Decision cost measured at ~180us in hot path (x86 server). Early microbench: 4-7% median latency improvement on H100, 10% on L40S for mixed-batch workloads.
2026-03-06: Observed a regression on A10 for sequences >4096 tokens due to smaller kernel memory assumptions; added kernel fallback and KV-cache warmup check to prototype.

2026-03-09: Design review with runtime team. Decision: keep arbitration logic tiered (fast heuristic then optional more expensive candidate scoring) to cap decision overhead. Agreed to default to heuristic in high-QPS paths and enable full scoring in low-QPS/diagnostic runs.
2026-03-12: Integration tests: end-to-end baseline vs arbiter on Dedicated staging: 95th percentile latency reduced by 11% across mixed fleets with no observed errors. Preparing canary rollout plan.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Heuristic-first vs full scoring: Chosen heuristic-first to limit decision overhead; full scoring gated by sampler flag. Reason: operations SLOs require <500us added latency budget.

Clock hints vs forced clock changes: We only emit soft clock-hint telemetry to the scheduler; runtime will not programmatically override clocks in hosted mode to avoid infra side effects. Private/Dedicated can opt-in to active governors via admin flag.
Determinism vs performance: Provide deterministic safe-fallback mode (single kernel variant) for customers who prefer predictable latency; default to adaptive for better unit economics.
Telemetry sampling: Full telemetry for every request is too expensive; we sample 1% of requests for full kernel-candidate scoring and aggregate lightweight counters for all requests.
review_feedback: Samantha Lee (Eng Lead) - 'Nice separation between heuristic and expensive scoring. Please add a tight microbenchmark to ensure 180us doesn't regress with additional metrics.'

Ethan Wu (PM) - 'Customer impact looks high for mixed-sku fleets. Add a canary plan and a rollback threshold (5% error or 12% tail latency increase). Also include a configurable knob for Dedicated customers to enable active clock steering.'
Design (Aisha Gomez) - 'Consider exposing a per-route policy in Console to prefer deterministic mode for latency-sensitive endpoints.'
acceptance_criteria: Arbitration decision adds <250us median overhead on hot path for 95% of requests
End-to-end canary shows <=1% increase in error rate and >=8% reduction in p95 latency for mixed-sku traces compared to baseline
Safe-fallback mode can be toggled without restart and documented in runbook
Bench dashboard updated with H100/L40S/A10 comparative sweeps and a nightly job to surface regressions
Feature flag and Console control exist for Dedicated/Private customers to enable active clock hints
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Added decision layer could become new source of latency — Mitigation: keep heuristic path in hot loop and add budgeted microbench alerts
Risk: Kernel mis-selection under unseen sequence distributions — Mitigation: sample full scoring with histograms, and maintain conservative default kernel
Risk: Clock hinting in multi-tenant MIG environments could cause noisy neighbor regressions — Mitigation: make active clock steering opt-in for Dedicated and rely on soft hints for Hosted
testing_and_benchmarks: Perf harness: /infra/perf/benchmarks/arbiter-sweep (sweeps across SKUs, MIG configs, seq-lens 32..8192)
Nightly: compare baseline runtime-1.21 vs runtime-1.22 arbiter using real production traces sampled from last 7 days
Canary: phased rollout to 5% traffic on Dedicated staging, measure p50/p95/p99, error rate, and kernel switch counts
comments: Miguel Ortega (2026-03-03): Ran extended L40S 16k token trace, found kernel switch thrash when thermals spike. Added hysteresis to decision layer.
Priya Nair (2026-03-07): Uploaded initial microbench results to Grafana. Observed A10 long-tail issue; added KV-cache warmup gate.
Samantha Lee (2026-03-10): Approved canary plan pending dashboard thresholds.
